title: Germany news: Merz to nominate Aigner for president
summary: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz announced that he will nominate Ilse Aigner for president, paving the way for her to be the first woman to hold the office. DW has more.
byline: Jon Shelton, Saim Dušan Inayatullah, Timothy Jones

image.caption: Aigner currently serves as the president of the Bavarian state parliamentImage: Sven Hoppe/dpa/picture alliance

blocks.text: Merz to nominate Aigner as Germany's next federal president

German Chancellor Friedrich Merz announced announced to the Christian Democrat Union (CDU) party heads his intention to nominate Ilse Aigner as the country's next federal president, according to the dpa, AFP and Reuters news agencies.
She will replace Frank-Walter Steinmeier when he steps down at the end of his term early next year.

Aigner, who hails from Bavaria's conservative Christian Social Union (CSU) and is the president of the Bavarian state parliament, would be the first woman to hold the German president's position should she be elected on January 30.
Steinmeier is a member of the junior coalition partner SPD.
Merz will officially pitch Aigner's name for the job on Monday, when party leaders will gather to choose a joint candidate.
SPD and Green Party representatives have already voiced support for her candidacy.
